metadata.name: Queueing lab: one service under load
metadata.description: A single service with 4 workers and exponential 10 ms service time (an M/M/4 queue, capacity 400 req/s). CPU and memory are not modelled (auto-sizing is off), so it behaves exactly like the textbook queue. Compare the scenarios to see latency explode near saturation, and how a queue timeout sheds load instead of wasting work on requests whose clients already gave up.

scenarios.name: 50% load (200 req/s)
scenarios.description: The document as drawn: half of capacity, so requests rarely wait.

scenarios.name: 90% load (360 req/s)
scenarios.description: Close to saturation: utilization rises linearly, waiting time does not.

scenarios.name: 110% load, unbounded queue
scenarios.description: Over capacity with an unbounded queue: the queue grows forever, clients time out, and the service keeps working on abandoned requests.

scenarios.name: 110% load, queue timeout 200 ms
scenarios.description: Same overload, but requests that wait more than 200 ms are rejected immediately, so capacity goes to requests that can still succeed.
